0.long_answer: Mycosis fungoides is the most common subtype of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (CTCL). CTCLs are a group of non-Hodgkin lymphomas that originate from T lymphocytes and primarily involve the skin. Although CTCL accounts for only about 2% of all cancers involving lymphocytes, Mycosis fungoides represents the most frequent form of these lymphomas, often leading to skin manifestations such as patches, plaques, and tumors.
